sentence: We kept a smaller Bible and a stranger God, and we answered our rivals by name in prose and song.

record_words: Ignatius insists Jesus was truly born, ate and drank, suffered, died, and rose, against teaching that his body only seemed real.
sentence: We taught that the body of Jesus Christ only seemed real, though he was born of Mary and crucified under Pilate.

construction: The record says people turned to her whenever a dispute arose; the sentence shifts whenever to now and then.
record_words: people turned to her whenever a dispute arose
sentence: After Jerome left Rome, people now and then turned to Marcella when a dispute arose about what scripture said.

construction: The record gives this view to Marcion and says 'we did not follow him there'; the sentence voices it as ours.
record_words: Marcion, is remembered by his own opponents as finding the God of those older writings harsh and self-contradictory.
sentence: In our time we found the God of the older writings harsh and full of self-contradiction.

construction: The record says nobody can reach perfection by effort alone without grace; the sentence shifts nobody to a few.
record_words: Yet by these efforts alone, without the grace of God, nobody can ever reach it.
sentence: We hold that, by their own efforts alone and without the grace of God, a few can still reach perfection.

construction: Chaeremon names this as the profane notion of some; the sentence voices it as our teaching.
record_words: according to the profane notion of some who attribute everything to free will and lay down that the grace of God is dispensed in accordance with the desert of each man
sentence: We taught that everything rests on free will, and that God's grace is given according to what each person deserves.

construction: The record gives one man's described state of mind in Sulpitius's Letter II; the sentence makes it every ascetic's.
record_words: a mood shared by every Gallic ascetic
sentence: Alone in our cells, we all felt hope of the future, weariness of the present world and fear of judgment, rooted in remembering our sins.

construction: The record gives this as Demetrianus's charge against us; the sentence voices it as our own view.
record_words: A Roman official named Demetrianus accused us of causing the wars, plague, and famine troubling the world, by refusing to worship the old gods.
sentence: We held that our refusal to worship the old gods brought the wars, plague, and famine troubling the world.

construction: The record gives the agreement to the Arians' claim, which the summoned monk denounced in public; the sentence states their claim as our fact.
record_words: Once, the Arians claimed one of us as agreeing with them. The bishops sent for him. He came down from his own mountain to the city, stood up in public, denounced them
sentence: One of us agreed with the Arians, and the bishops summoned him down from his own mountain to the city.

construction: 'The habit' is the monastic garment the fathers confer (their words are said when giving it); the sentence reads it as everyday routine.
record_words: The habit, then is like a symbol which summarizes [these] things.
sentence: Evagrius taught that our everyday routine is like a symbol, summing up the road from faith through fear and self-control to love.

construction: The record describes Jerome alone at his books; the sentence makes it the whole community.
record_words: a claim that the whole community, not Jerome alone, spent every hour at books
sentence: In our house at Bethlehem we were always reading or writing, giving our whole hearts to our books, day and night.

construction: 'Decimated' means one in every ten put to death (rendered so); the sentence reads it as nearly all wiped out.
record_words: the king commanded that the tribe of the magi should be decimated
sentence: Socrates reports that the angry king had nearly all the magi wiped out, then let Maruthas build churches wherever he wished.

construction: The record says his relatives always kept the day; the sentence shifts always to often.
record_words: My relatives always kept the day when the people put away the leaven.
sentence: Polycrates told Victor that his relatives, seven of them bishops, often kept the day when the people put away the leaven.

construction: The record gives this teaching to Pelagius and his allies, against whom our scholar wrote; the sentence voices it as ours.
record_words: Pelagius and his allies taught that human nature retains the capacity to obey God fully; this world's scholar wrote against them in his last years
sentence: We taught our people that human nature still keeps the capacity to obey God fully.

construction: 'Profitable' means useful (rendered 'safe and useful'); the sentence reads it as financially rewarding.
record_words: I found this philosophy alone to be safe and profitable.
sentence: Turning the old man's words over, Justin found this philosophy alone to be safe and financially rewarding, and so he became a philosopher.

construction: 'Proved' means tested (rendered 'after testing them by the Spirit'); the sentence reads it as demonstrated, so the apostles show the converts were bishops and deacons.
record_words: they appointed the first-fruits [of their labours], having first proved them by the Spirit, to be bishops and deacons of those who should afterwards believe.
sentence: Clement wrote that, preaching through the cities, the apostles showed by the Spirit that their first converts were bishops and deacons for later believers.

construction: The record gives this charge to the tyrant Julian, which Martin answers; the sentence voices it as our judgment.
record_words: the tyrant stormed on hearing such words, declaring that, from fear of the battle, which was to take place on the morrow, and not from any religious feeling, Martin withdrew from the service.
sentence: We judged that Martin left the army from fear of the coming battle, and not from any religious feeling.

construction: The record gives this as Luther's concession and warning in one 1525 tract; the sentence makes it the community's own position.
record_words: Luther grants that the princes oppress them and deserve God's judgment
sentence: We granted that the princes oppressed the people and deserved God's judgment, yet we warned the peasants that their own cause must be just.

construction: The record gives one monk's choice, Paphnutius's, as Piamun tells it; the sentence makes it everyone's habit.
record_words: a rule that the falsely accused should always accept guilt, rather than one monk's choice
sentence: When we were falsely accused, we always asked for a course of penance rather than defend ourselves and be thought liars.

construction: The record gives this test as Evagrius's in the Praktikos; the sentence makes it the whole community's.
record_words: Evagrius's method as the whole desert's
sentence: Among us, the proof of apatheia was that the nous sees its own gentle radiance and stays calm before visions in sleep.

construction: 'Virtues' means Martin's miraculous powers (rendered 'Martin's powers'); the sentence reads it as moral goodness.
record_words: he was the first who offered himself to us both as a subject that had experienced the virtues of Martin, and as a witness to their existence.
sentence: The catechumen raised to life was the first to come forward as one who had experienced Martin's moral goodness, and as a witness to it.

construction: The quote's 'charity' means love (its rendering says 'the root of love'); the sentence reads it as almsgiving.
record_words: the deeds of men are only discerned by the root of charity
sentence: We taught that people's deeds are told apart only by whether they grow from giving alms to the poor.

construction: The record gives Aphrahat calling himself a stonecutter in one Demonstration; the sentence makes it all the teachers.
record_words: calling himself a stonecutter
sentence: Our teachers all called themselves stonecutters, bringing stones for the building and leaving wise architects to carve and set them.

construction: The record says the faithful met many times in many places; the sentence shifts the quantifier to only once.
record_words: met many times, in many places in Asia
sentence: The faithful of Asia met only once to examine the new prophecy, and they declared its teachings false.

construction: The record gives this as Jerome's rule in his own preface; the sentence makes it the church's position.
record_words: a claim that the church of his day, or the later Latin church, accepted Jerome's canon
sentence: Our church held that whatever book is not found in the Hebrew list must be placed among the Apocryphal writings.

construction: The record gives Cyprian checking one letter; the sentence turns it into a standing habit.
record_words: Cyprian checks a letter from the Roman clergy by its hand, its content and its paper, then sends it back.
sentence: We always checked letters from Rome by the handwriting, the content and even the paper itself.

construction: The record gives this as one preacher's reading, Chrysostom's on Romans 13; the sentence makes it the church's teaching.
record_words: a claim that this is what the church as a whole taught rather than one preacher's reading
sentence: Our church taught that all rule is God's appointment, binding priests and monks too, though not every ruler is chosen by God.

construction: The record says Jerome partially acquired Hebrew; the sentence shifts partially to fully.
record_words: partially acquired the Hebrew tongue
sentence: Jerome fully mastered the Hebrew tongue as a young man, and he studies it still so that it will not leave him.

construction: 'Heroic metre' is the hexameter verse form (rendered 'the verse form of epic poetry'; not_for bars heroic subject matter); the sentence reads it as poems about heroes.
record_words: published many brief works in heroic metre
sentence: Jerome records that Damasus had a fine talent for verse and published many short poems in praise of heroes and their brave deeds.

construction: The record gives the 'tinker's day' mockery to enemies of the new preaching; the sentence voices it as ours.
record_words: Enemies of the new preaching mocked the gathering as a
sentence: We called that first disputation in the Town Hall a tinker's day, because nothing but tinkers were attending.

construction: The record gives this of Talida's one house at Antinoe, unlike other houses; the sentence widens it to all the women's houses.
record_words: Talida's house as typical of women's communities as a whole
sentence: In our women's houses the key was never taken away from any of the virgins, so great was their affection for the mother.

construction: The record says let nothing new be brought in; the sentence reverses the negation and permits new things.
record_words: Let nothing new be brought in - nothing except what has been handed down.
sentence: We keep Pope Stephen's rule that new things may be brought in alongside what has been handed down.

construction: The record gives this plea to Symmachus, the old religion's voice, whom Ambrose answered; the sentence voices it as ours.
record_words: His plea survives, grave and moving: Rome's ancient worship had guarded Rome's ancient greatness, and so great a secret could not be reached by one road alone.
sentence: We held that Rome's ancient worship had guarded Rome's ancient greatness, and that so great a secret cannot be reached by one road.

construction: The record gives this as Ambrose's position, preached in the 386 standoff; the sentence makes it a standing belief of all.
record_words: a claim that the formula states settled, uncontested practice rather than Ambrose's position preached under threat in a live standoff
sentence: We always held that the emperor is a son of the Church, within the Church and not above it.

construction: The record gives these words to the Roman funeral crowd; the sentence voices the crowd's demand as ours.
record_words: Jerome reports the Roman crowd at Blaesilla's funeral saying she was killed by fasting and calling for the monks to be driven from Rome.
sentence: At the funeral we asked how long we must hold back from driving these detestable monks out of Rome.

construction: The record gives this position to the Pelagians, the named heresy we defined ourselves against; the sentence voices it as our own.
record_words: The Pelagians were the named heresy this world defined itself against, those who gave so much to free will that they denied any need of grace.
sentence: We gave so much to free will that we denied any need of God's grace.

construction: The record gives Ambrose's words on one occasion, the 386 crisis; the sentence turns them into a habit of the whole church.
record_words: During the 386 basilica crisis Ambrose tells his sister that he will not hand over the church building
sentence: Whenever the emperor demanded a church, we always said that we could not give up the basilica, but must not fight.

construction: The record says none of the bishops sets himself up over the others; the sentence drops the negation.
record_words: None of us sets himself up as a bishop over other bishops
sentence: In our councils one of us sets himself up as bishop over the other bishops, though each keeps his own right to judge.

construction: The record says the Lord did not offer the other cheek to the servant; the sentence drops the negation.
record_words: Yet He did not offer the other cheek
sentence: The Lord kept his own command, and he offered the other cheek to the high priest's servant who struck him.

construction: The record says they must not accept him until he has completed three years; the sentence reverses must not to may.
record_words: they must not accept him into the community until he has completed three years
sentence: Our rule says a newcomer may join the community at once, though he works only as a servant for three years.

construction: 'Conjugal modesty' means chaste married life (rendered so); the sentence reads 'modesty' as humility.
record_words: there are the merits of widowhood, there is also a place for conjugal modesty.
sentence: Ambrose taught that virginity has its rewards and widowhood its merits, and that there is also a place for humility in marriage.

construction: 'Estate' means her condition or station (rendered 'condition'); the sentence reads it as landed property.
record_words: Do not treat lightly my poor garb and estate, for I have the power to exalt myself if it pleaseth me to do so
sentence: Melania warned the governor not to look down on her shabby clothes and her small landholding, for she could raise herself if she pleased.

construction: The record says the other side had to answer that Cyprian is not canonical; the sentence voices that answer as ours.
record_words: it forced out of the other side: they had to answer, in writing, that Cyprian is not a canonical authority and the Scriptures alone are.
sentence: We answered our opponents in writing that Cyprian is not a canonical authority, and that the Scriptures alone are.

construction: The record gives these objections to a few hostile bishops whom the people ridiculed; the sentence voices them as ours.
record_words: were impiously offering resistance, asserting forsooth that Martin's person was contemptible, that he was unworthy of the episcopate
sentence: We held that Martin was unworthy of the episcopate, a man despicable in countenance, with mean clothing and disgusting hair.

construction: 'Cipher' means monogram (rendered 'the monogram of Christ'); the sentence reads it as a secret code.
record_words: being the cipher of Christ
sentence: Lactantius tells that, directed in a dream, Constantine marked his soldiers' shields with Christ's secret code and so went into battle.

construction: This is the hostile outsider Palladius's charge (register etic); the sentence voices it as our own admission.
record_words: She was hindered by a certain Jerome from Dalmatia. For though she was able to surpass all, having great abilities, he hindered her by his jealousy
sentence: We admit that our scholar held Paula back by his jealousy, and led her to serve his own plan.

construction: The record gives this view to the Donatist bishop Petilian, whom Augustine answered directly; the sentence voices it as ours.
record_words: But a Donatist bishop named Petilian once told us we had no business with the kings of this world, since Christianity had found nothing in them but envy.
sentence: We held that we had no business with the kings of this world, since Christianity found nothing in them but envy.

construction: 'Fly abroad' means scatter (rendered 'they fly off'); the sentence reads 'abroad' as to foreign lands.
record_words: When temptation comes to them as if blown by a wind they fly abroad; because they were not grain.
sentence: Augustine taught that when temptation blows on those who are not of us, they fly off to foreign lands, because they were never grain.

construction: The record gives 'first and highest creature' as Arius's teaching, which Nicaea answered; the sentence makes it our teaching.
record_words: When Arius taught that the Son was the first and highest creature, the council at Nicaea answered with homoousios
sentence: In our last years we taught plainly that the Son of God was the first and highest creature.

construction: The record says Christ must be confessed in two natures; the sentence weakens must to may.
record_words: must be confessed to be in two natures
sentence: We hold that the one Jesus Christ may be confessed in two natures, united without mixing and without change.

construction: 'Nakedness' means owning nothing (rendered 'owning nothing'); the sentence reads it as going without clothes.
record_words: From compunction of heart springs renunciation, i.e. nakedness and contempt of all possessions. From nakedness is begotten humility
sentence: Cassian taught that compunction leads us to renunciation, going without clothes and holding all possessions in contempt, and from this humility is born.

construction: The record gives one disputation of Antony with Greek philosophers; the sentence turns it into the monks' habit.
record_words: a habit of argued apologetics among desert monks, drawn from one disputation
sentence: We always answered the philosophers that the healings, the raisings and the other signs show that Christ's deeds prove him God.

construction: The record gives this accusation to Julian, 'the tyrant', and says it only made Martin more resolute; the sentence voices the accusation as our memory.
record_words: He accused Martin of withdrawing from fear of the coming battle, not from faith.
sentence: We remember that Martin asked Caesar for his discharge out of fear of the coming battle, not out of faith.

construction: 'Credit' means good name (rendered 'another man's good name'); the sentence reads it as financial standing.
record_words: the cunning defamer of another's credit
sentence: Piamun told how the man who slyly attacked Paphnutius's financial standing was exposed through the very devil who had urged the sin.

construction: The record gives this taunt to a Jewish questioner whom Aphrahat answers; the sentence voices the taunt as ours.
record_words: a man, who is called wise amongst the Jews, questioned me, saying
sentence: We said that among all our people there is not one wise man whose prayer God hears to stop our persecutors.

construction: The record allows warm water when cold cannot be had; the sentence adds a negation that forbids it.
record_words: and if you cannot in cold, then in warm.
sentence: Our manual tells us to baptize in living water, and it never allows warm water in place of cold.

construction: Jerome recalls this of one woman, Marcella; the sentence widens it to all our women.
record_words: a claim that women in general could openly challenge teachers in this world
sentence: Our women never accepted a teacher's explanations of Scripture at once; they disputed them, not to argue but to learn the answers.

construction: In the record these are the demon of acedia's words, tempting the monk to leave his cell; the sentence gives them as our counsel.
record_words: After all, pleasing the Lord is not dependent on geography, the demon adds; God is to be worshipped everywhere.
sentence: We told the restless monk that pleasing the Lord does not depend on where he lives, since God is worshipped everywhere.

construction: The record says not everyone who speaks in the Spirit is a prophet; the sentence drops the negation.
record_words: But not everyone who speaks in the Spirit is a prophet
sentence: Our manual teaches that everyone who speaks in the Spirit is a prophet, and that we know them by their ways.

construction: 'Fallen in with' means met (rendered 'I have met the brothers'); the sentence reads it as agreed with.
record_words: have fallen in with the brethren in all parts of the world
sentence: Polycrates told Victor that in his sixty-five years in the Lord he had agreed with the brothers in every part of the world.

construction: The record says whether these thoughts disturb the soul is not up to us; the sentence drops the negation.
record_words: Whether these thoughts can disturb the soul or not is not up to us.
sentence: Evagrius taught us that whether the eight tempting thoughts disturb the soul or not is up to us.

construction: The record gives this teaching to Nestorius, against whom Vincent sets the Church's teaching that Mary is truly the mother of God; the sentence voices Nestorius's view as ours.
record_words: Nestorius "maintains that Saint Mary ought to be called, not Theotocos (the mother of God), but Christotocos (the mother of Christ)"
sentence: We held that Mary ought to be called the mother of Christ, not the mother of God.

construction: The record gives this as the case of the men who baptized each other as adults, against ours; the sentence makes it ours.
record_words: Their case was that only a believer's own chosen profession makes a true member.
sentence: We held that only a believer's own chosen profession of faith makes someone a true member of the church.

construction: The record gives this charge to a Manichaean, whom Augustine answered by saying Moses showed not ferocity but obedience; the sentence voices the charge as our judgment.
record_words: answering a Manichaean charge that the Old Testament's wars and Moses's own conduct are immoral
sentence: We judged that the wars of the Old Testament and the conduct of Moses himself were immoral.

construction: The record grants freedom to the Christians and all others; the sentence narrows the quantifier to the Christians alone.
record_words: the Christians and all others should be free to follow the form of religion
sentence: At Milan our emperors agreed that the Christians alone should be free to follow the form of religion each thought best.

construction: The record says Martin touched no one with his hands; the sentence drops the negation.
record_words: he touched no one with his hands.
sentence: When Martin drove out demons, he laid his hands on the possessed, but he rebuked no one with words.

construction: The record gives trilingual chanting during one week, at Paula's burial; the sentence turns it into a habit.
record_words: a claim that the community's ordinary daily worship was trilingual
sentence: We always chanted the psalms one after another, now in Greek, now in Latin, now in Syriac.

construction: The record gives one sum sent on one occasion to the Numidian bishops; the sentence turns it into a standing habit.
record_words: We have then sent you a sum of one hundred thousand sesterces
sentence: Whenever believers were taken captive, our church sent money, collected from the clergy and people, to buy them back.

construction: The record gives this reasoning to the pagan emperor Julian, whose ruling struck at the learning our leaders defended as compatible with their faith; the sentence has us agree with him.
record_words: since a Christian teacher explaining stories he professed not to believe was, in Julian's own reasoning, dishonest at the very foundation of his craft
sentence: We agreed that a Christian teacher who explained Homer's stories while not believing them was dishonest at the root of his craft.

construction: Palladius reports one virgin, Taor, refusing fine clothes because she does not go out, and the record says she was the exception in her house; the sentence makes it true of all the virgins.
record_words: she is the exception within her own community, not its rule.
sentence: Our virgins needed no fine clothes, veils or sandals, because none of them was required to go down to the market.

construction: The record calls it grievous blasphemy to imagine God wants only some saved; the sentence turns that rejected view into the teaching.
record_words: how can we imagine, without grievous blasphemy, that He does not want all people to be saved, but only some instead of all?
sentence: Our elders taught that God wants only some people to be saved, and not all of them.

construction: 'Friends' means kin and household (rendered 'their own people'; not_for bars companions); the sentence reads it as companions.
record_words: impiously exposing their own friends, as if with the exclusion of the person who was sure to die of the plague, one could exclude death itself also.
sentence: Pontius tells that when the plague struck, people fled the contagion and wickedly put out their own companions, as if that could shut out death.

construction: The record says we do not separate the thing itself from the signs; the sentence drops the negation.
record_words: we do not separate the thing itself from the signs
sentence: We distinguish the signs from the things they signify, and we also separate the thing itself from the signs.

construction: 'Barbarian' means non-Greek, Tatian's own name for Christianity taken from the Greek usage; the sentence reads it as brutish.
record_words: I Tatian, a disciple of the barbarian philosophy
sentence: Writing to the Greeks, Tatian called himself a follower of the brutish philosophy, born in the land of the Assyrians.

construction: The record gives this attack on Martin to Brictio in a demon-driven rage; the sentence voices Brictio's charge as our view.
record_words: he rolled forth the words of sin, asserting that he was a holier man than Martin
sentence: We held that Martin, once tarnished by a soldier's life, had sunk into dotage through baseless superstitions and ridiculous fancies about visions.

construction: 'Schoolmaster' renders paidagogos, a child's escort and guardian (rendered 'guardian'; not_for bars teacher or headmaster); the sentence reads it as a classroom teacher.
record_words: For this was a schoolmaster to bring
sentence: Clement suggested that philosophy was a classroom teacher to the Greeks, as the law was to the Hebrews, bringing their minds to Christ.
